14: /-!
15: # `p`-adic Valuation
16: 
17: This file defines the `p`-adic valuation on `ℕ`, `ℤ`, and `ℚ`.
18: 
19: The `p`-adic valuation on `ℚ` is the difference of the multiplicities of `p` in the numerator and
20: denominator of `q`. This function obeys the standard properties of a valuation, with the appropriate
21: assumptions on `p`. The `p`-adic valuations on `ℕ` and `ℤ` agree with that on `ℚ`.
22: 
23: The valuation induces a norm on `ℚ`. This norm is defined in
24: `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/PadicNorm.lean`.
25: 
26: ## Notation
27: 
28: This file uses the local notation `/.` for `Rat.mk`.
29: 
30: ## Implementation notes
31: 
32: Much, but not all, of this file assumes that `p` is prime. This assumption is inferred automatically
33: by taking `[Fact p.Prime]` as a type class argument.
34: 
35: ## Calculations with `p`-adic valuations
36: 
37: * `padicValNat_factorial`: Legendre's Theorem. The `p`-adic valuation of `n!` is the sum of the
38:   quotients `n / p ^ i`. This sum is expressed over the finset `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound
39:   greater than `log p n`. See `Nat.Prime.multiplicity_factorial` for the same result but stated in
40:   the language of prime multiplicity.
41: 
42: * `sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial`: Legendre's Theorem.  Taking (`p - 1`) times
43:   the `p`-adic valuation of `n!` equals `n` minus the sum of base `p` digits of `n`.
44: 
45: * `padicValNat_choose`: Kummer's Theorem. The `p`-adic valuation of `n.choose k` is the number
46:   of carries when `k` and `n - k` are added in base `p`. This sum is expressed over the finset
47:   `Ico 1 b` where `b` is any bound greater than `log p n`. See `Nat.Prime.multiplicity_choose` for
48:   the same result but stated in the language of prime multiplicity.
49: 
50: * `sub_one_mul_padicValNat_choose_eq_sub_sum_digits`: Kummer's Theorem. Taking (`p - 1`) times the
51:   `p`-adic valuation of the binomial `n` over `k` equals the sum of the digits of `k` plus the sum
52:   of the digits of `n - k` minus the sum of digits of `n`, all base `p`.
53: 
54: ## References
55: 
56: * [F. Q. Gouvêa, *p-adic numbers*][gouvea1997]
57: * [R. Y. Lewis, *A formal proof of Hensel's lemma over the p-adic integers*][lewis2019]
58: * <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P-adic_number>
59:

note.fact: For prime integer p and every nonzero rational q, there exist eta in Z and a unit u of R=Z_(p) such that q=p^eta u. For a nonempty finite family of such exponents, its minimum nu is attained, and p^(eta_j-nu) belongs to R for each j.

grounds.reason: p is prime, hence p>=2 and p is nonzero.
Fractions with denominator prime to p are exactly the given elements of R.
The coefficients are nonzero rational numbers in a nonempty finite generating list.

note.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Repeatedly remove factors p from A and B; this terminates because their nonzero absolute values decrease at each division by p>=2. Write A=p^s A' and B=p^t B', with A',B' prime to p. Then eta=s-t and u=A'/B'; both u and its inverse lie in R. A finite nonempty list of integers has an attained minimum. Each eta_j-nu is nonnegative, so the corresponding power of p is integral and belongs to R. This verifies the factorization and minimum step already used by S004–S005.

202: /-- The multiplicity of `p : ℕ` in `a : ℤ` is finite exactly when `a ≠ 0`. -/
203: theorem finite_int_prime_iff {a : ℤ} : FiniteMultiplicity (p : ℤ) a ↔ a ≠ 0 := by
204:   simp [Int.finiteMultiplicity_iff, hp.1.ne_one]
205: 
206: /-- A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p q` when `q` is expressed in terms of `Rat.mk`. -/
207: protected theorem defn (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {q : ℚ} {n d : ℤ} (hqz : q ≠ 0)
208:     (qdf : q = n /. d) :
209:     padicValRat p q = multiplicity (p : ℤ) n - multiplicity (p : ℤ) d := by
210:   have hd : d ≠ 0 := Rat.mk_denom_ne_zero_of_ne_zero hqz qdf
211:   let ⟨c, hc1, hc2⟩ := Rat.num_den_mk hd qdf
212:   rw [padicValRat.multiplicity_sub_multiplicity hp.1.ne_one hqz]
213:   simp only [hc1, hc2]
214:   rw [multiplicity_mul (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1),
215:     multiplicity_mul (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1)]
216:   · rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_add]
217:     simp_rw [Int.natCast_multiplicity p q.den]
218:     ring
219:   · simpa [finite_int_prime_iff, hc2] using hd
220:   · simpa [finite_int_prime_iff, hqz, hc2] using hd
221: 
222: /-- A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q * r)` with conditions `q ≠ 0`, `r ≠ 0`. -/
223: protected theorem mul {q r : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hr : r ≠ 0) :
224:     padicValRat p (q * r) = padicValRat p q + padicValRat p r := by
225:   have : q * r = (q.num * r.num) /. (q.den * r.den) := by
226:     rw [Rat.mul_eq_mkRat, Rat.mkRat_eq_divInt, Nat.cast_mul]
227:   have hq' : q.num /. q.den ≠ 0 := by rwa [Rat.num_divInt_den]
228:   have hr' : r.num /. r.den ≠ 0 := by rwa [Rat.num_divInt_den]
229:   have hp' : Prime (p : ℤ) := Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1
230:   rw [padicValRat.defn p (mul_ne_zero hq hr) this]
231:   conv_rhs =>
232:     rw [← q.num_divInt_den, padicValRat.defn p hq', ← r.num_divInt_den, padicValRat.defn p hr']
233:   rw [multiplicity_mul hp', multiplicity_mul hp', Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_add]
234:   · ring
235:   · simp [finite_int_prime_iff]
236:   · simp [finite_int_prime_iff, hq, hr]

238: /-- A rewrite lemma for `padicValRat p (q^k)`. -/
239: @[simp]
240: protected theorem pow (q : ℚ) {k : ℕ} :
241:     padicValRat p (q ^ k) = k * padicValRat p q := by
242:   obtain rfl | hq := eq_or_ne q 0
243:   · cases k <;> simp
244:   induction k <;>
245:     simp [*, padicValRat.mul hq (pow_ne_zero _ hq), _root_.pow_succ', add_mul, add_comm]

249: protected theorem inv (q : ℚ) : padicValRat p q⁻¹ = -padicValRat p q := by
250:   by_cases hq : q = 0
251:   · simp [hq]
252:   · rw [eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero, ← padicValRat.mul (inv_ne_zero hq) hq, inv_mul_cancel₀ hq,

261: protected theorem div {q r : ℚ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hr : r ≠ 0) :
262:     padicValRat p (q / r) = padicValRat p q - padicValRat p r := by
263:   rw [div_eq_mul_inv, padicValRat.mul hq (inv_ne_zero hr), padicValRat.inv r, sub_eq_add_neg]

265: /-- A condition for `padicValRat p (n₁ / d₁) ≤ padicValRat p (n₂ / d₂)`, in terms of
266: divisibility by `p^n`. -/
267: theorem padicValRat_le_padicValRat_iff {n₁ n₂ d₁ d₂ : ℤ} (hn₁ : n₁ ≠ 0) (hn₂ : n₂ ≠ 0)
268:     (hd₁ : d₁ ≠ 0) (hd₂ : d₂ ≠ 0) :
269:     padicValRat p (n₁ /. d₁) ≤ padicValRat p (n₂ /. d₂) ↔
270:       ∀ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ n ∣ n₁ * d₂ → (p : ℤ) ^ n ∣ n₂ * d₁ := by
271:   have hf1 : FiniteMultiplicity (p : ℤ) (n₁ * d₂) := finite_int_prime_iff.2 (mul_ne_zero hn₁ hd₂)
272:   have hf2 : FiniteMultiplicity (p : ℤ) (n₂ * d₁) := finite_int_prime_iff.2 (mul_ne_zero hn₂ hd₁)
273:   conv =>
274:     lhs
275:     rw [padicValRat.defn p (Rat.divInt_ne_zero_of_ne_zero hn₁ hd₁) rfl,
276:       padicValRat.defn p (Rat.divInt_ne_zero_of_ne_zero hn₂ hd₂) rfl, sub_le_iff_le_add', ←
277:       add_sub_assoc, le_sub_iff_add_le]
278:     norm_cast
279:     rw [← multiplicity_mul (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1) hf1, add_comm,
280:         ← multiplicity_mul (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1) hf2,
281:         hf1.multiplicity_le_multiplicity_iff hf2]

283: /-- Sufficient conditions to show that the `p`-adic valuation of `q` is less than or equal to the
284: `p`-adic valuation of `q + r`. -/
285: theorem le_padicValRat_add_of_le {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0)
286:     (h : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p r) : padicValRat p q ≤ padicValRat p (q + r) :=
287:   if hq : q = 0 then by simpa [hq] using h
288:   else
289:     if hr : r = 0 then by simp [hr]
290:     else by
291:       have hqn : q.num ≠ 0 := Rat.num_ne_zero.2 hq
292:       have hqd : (q.den : ℤ) ≠ 0 := mod_cast Rat.den_nz _
293:       have hrn : r.num ≠ 0 := Rat.num_ne_zero.2 hr
294:       have hrd : (r.den : ℤ) ≠ 0 := mod_cast Rat.den_nz _
295:       have hqreq : q + r = (q.num * r.den + q.den * r.num) /. (q.den * r.den) := Rat.add_num_den _ _
296:       have hqrd : q.num * r.den + q.den * r.num ≠ 0 := Rat.mk_num_ne_zero_of_ne_zero hqr hqreq
297:       conv_lhs => rw [← q.num_divInt_den]
298:       rw [hqreq, padicValRat_le_padicValRat_iff hqn hqrd hqd (mul_ne_zero hqd hrd), ←
299:         emultiplicity_le_emultiplicity_iff, mul_left_comm,
300:         emultiplicity_mul (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1), add_mul]
301:       rw [← q.num_divInt_den, ← r.num_divInt_den, padicValRat_le_padicValRat_iff hqn hrn hqd hrd, ←
302:         emultiplicity_le_emultiplicity_iff] at h
303:       calc
304:         _ ≤ min (emultiplicity ↑p (q.num * r.den * q.den))
305:                 (emultiplicity ↑p (q.den * r.num * q.den)) :=
306:           le_min
307:             (by rw [emultiplicity_mul (a := _ * _) (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1), add_comm])
308:             (by grw [mul_assoc, emultiplicity_mul (b := _ * _) (Nat.prime_iff_prime_int.1 hp.1), h])
309:         _ ≤ _ := min_le_emultiplicity_add

311: /-- The minimum of the valuations of `q` and `r` is at most the valuation of `q + r`. -/
312: theorem min_le_padicValRat_add {q r : ℚ} (hqr : q + r ≠ 0) :
313:     min (padicValRat p q) (padicValRat p r) ≤ padicValRat p (q + r) :=
314:   (le_total (padicValRat p q) (padicValRat p r)).elim
315:   (fun h => by rw [min_eq_left h]; exact le_padicValRat_add_of_le hqr h)
316:   (fun h => by rw [min_eq_right h, add_comm]; exact le_padicValRat_add_of_le (by rwa [add_comm]) h)
